effect: Devaluing a peg costs credibility and can no longer be repeated at once. The player's devalue action ($mQ, the only caller; AI countries never devalue, they float) is refused for 180 days after a devaluation (reason cooldown; the monetary view marks the action unavailable with reasonId cooldown, which the money panel shows as its generic refusal text), and each devaluation now also cuts the monetary credibility anchor (country.anchor, the game's own 0-to-anchor0 credibility that sets bond yields at +12 points and the rating at +8 notches per unit lost, and how fast inflation expectations follow inflation) of every member of the currency by 5% of its level, plus 5% more for each other devaluation of that currency in the last 3 years (5%, 10%, 15% ..., at most 30%), floored at the game's 0.02. Real repeated devaluations destroy the credibility of the new parity: a first realignment can be believed, a second within months tells the market to expect a third. The cut is the size of the game's own credibility hit for printing about 0.23% of GDP (G9A: anchor x exp(-0.219 x % of GDP)); the anchor then recovers toward its target at the game's own rate (0.3 a year of the gap), so a single devaluation fades over a few years while repeated ones compound. The game's own -3 approval, -2 stability and the 15% step are unchanged. End to end (tests/m6.headless.mjs, Denmark, seed 12345): the first devaluation cuts the anchor of Denmark, the Faroe Islands and Greenland from 1 to 0.95, a second the same day is refused, and on day 180 (anchors back to 0.953) the second devaluation cuts 10% to 0.858. State: sovereign.geobalDevaluations, the list of devaluation days pruned to 3 years when written (the currency object would lose a new field at save); absent in old saves (treated as no devaluation). Day 0 unchanged: no devaluation has happened, views only read. Not done: revaluing foreign-currency debt (not checked whether the game already does it through the exchange rate). Minified names are those of build 26318758.
